From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - token economics, caching & eval window

Maya — thanks for the note. I've attached a first-pass MAP worksheet (RDW-MAP-draft.xlsx) and summarized the key econ assumptions below so finance has a concise view.

High-level econ assumptions (pilot / MAP baseline):
- Unit: tokens per USD (tokens/$) baseline: 12,500 tokens per $1 at 8-bit quantized 13B variant under continuous batching and warm KV cache.
- Caching: we model a 40% effective prefix/KV cache hit rate for Acme's Q&A flows (histor prompt overlap + session affinity). Cache TTL for eligibility: 24h; cacheable = repeated system+user prefixes up to 512 tokens.
- Batching: typical steady-state batch size avg=6 (range 4-12). We assume an ops-configured max batch of 24 for micro-bursts; that affects latency tail but improves tokens/$ during peaks.
- Throughput assumptions: baseline throughput target = 120 reqs/s steady (20% concurrency headroom). For canary, we recommend a staged ramp to 300 reqs/s peak to validate burst handling.
- Quality/quantization trade: 8-bit QC shows ~1.5% top-line metric delta on our eval set versus FP16; we include a quality buffer in pricing for the first 30 days.

What we included in the attached XLS:
- Rows that model tokens/$ under three quantization profiles (FP16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and three cache hit scenarios (20%, 40%, 60%).
- Sensitivity table showing monthly cost delta for 100M tokens/month and 1B tokens/month.
- Canary run checklist + acceptance criteria (latency SLOs, 99p token cost variance < 12%).

Actions we need from Acme:
1) Confirm sample traffic profile (avg tokens per convo, session re-use percentage).
2) Approve the proposed 3-day canary window and target peak load dates.
3) Tell us if procurement needs the MAP as an exportable CSV for the PO attachment.

We'll be ready to iterate quickly — Jonas and Ben are looped for ops/throughput stuff.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RDW-MAP-draft.xlsx (workbook with sensitivity tabs)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff - token economics, caching & eval window

Maya — quick operational clarifications from my side so the MAP numbers line up with real traffic: 

Key asks from infra/ops for accurate runs:
- Peak concurrency pattern: do you have a 95th percentile concurrency and an expected RPS distribution (we need 95% and 99% windows).
- Cold vs warm: what percent of sessions will be returning users (we used 55% as a placeholder in the XLS).
- Response length distribution: are you mostly short calls (~150 tokens) or long form (~800+ tokens)? This changes tokens/$ dramatically.

Notes on canary design: 
- Recommend a 3-stage canary across two regions (us-west, us-east) across 5 calendar days: 24h smoke, 48h ramp, 24h peak verification. Our acceptance: 99p latency within 1.5x of baseline and cost per token within expected model variance.
- We'll enable KV-prefix caching and instrument raw cache hit metrics; please confirm you can pass a sample session id so we can track dedup rates.

I've dropped a starter troubleshooting runbook and a Drive link into the MAP folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0Bzrdw/rdw-acme-econ (public within the thread).

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference
